reason: E1 shows glass-to-glass transitions in high-entropy metallic glasses with improved thermal stability, but it describes a transition occurring during heating (not isothermal annealing) and in a different alloy system (NbNiZrTiCo, not P-containing). The specific premise that isothermal annealing at Tg−5 K induces such a transition in a P-containing HEA is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: High-entropy metallic glasses can undergo a glass-to-glass transition with large heat release.
Such a transition involves dramatic atomic rearrangement with short- and medium-range ordering.
The transition improves thermal stability (e.g., raises crystallization onset).
Isothermal annealing just below Tg can induce this transition in a phosphorus-containing HEA.
